questions.q: What is the core architectural difference between native reports and CRM Analytics?
options: Reports store data in datasets; CRM Analytics queries records live
Reports are only available in Classic; CRM Analytics is only in Lightning
Reports query live records when run; CRM Analytics queries prepared datasets loaded on a schedule
There is no architectural difference, only a different color theme
questions.explain: Native reports read live Salesforce records at run time. CRM Analytics reads datasets that were extracted and prepared ahead of time, so its data is only as fresh as the last refresh.

questions.q: What does faceting mean in a CRM Analytics dashboard?
options: Selecting a value in one widget re-slices other widgets that share the same data
Splitting a dataset into multiple apps
Adding a picture to the dashboard header
Scheduling the dashboard to refresh nightly
questions.explain: Faceting is the cross-widget interactivity where a selection in one chart filters the others. A native dashboard component runs its own report and does not filter its neighbors when clicked.

questions.q: A sales manager wants a simple list of one rep's open opportunities that is always current. What is the best fit?
options: A recipe that blends three external systems
A native Salesforce report
A custom SAQL dashboard with bindings
A new dataset with a nightly refresh
questions.explain: Simple operational needs are best served by a native report: fast to build, always current, and using inherited sharing with no data prep.

questions.q: Which trade-off comes with choosing CRM Analytics over a native report?
options: It cannot show charts
It cannot combine data from more than one object
It can only be used by system administrators
It brings data prep, refresh scheduling, deliberate security setup, and typically a separate license
questions.explain: CRM Analytics gains scale, blending, and interactivity but adds recipes or dataflows to maintain, refresh schedules, security configured on datasets, and a licensing decision.

questions.q: Which request most clearly justifies CRM Analytics over a native report?
options: A dashboard that blends CRM data with an external system and lets executives explore it interactively
A list of accounts created this week
A count of open cases by owner on a record page
A one-time export of contacts
questions.explain: Blending outside data and supporting deep interactive exploration are exactly what native reports do not do well, which is where CRM Analytics earns its added complexity.
